subject: how to override several scatter plots in the same coordinates

messages.author: 1e484235c6201bb6
messages.subject: how to override several scatter plots in the same coordinates
parts:
Dear ggploters,

I need your kind helps on how to override several scatter plots in the
same coordinates. I have two objective variables ("a" and "b") and
their own backgrounds ("abackground","bbackground"). I want to plot
all these four variables in the same coordinates, with the background
ones in the lower layers in grey colors and the objective ones in the
upper layers in bright colors. I have tried following the clue of the
ggplot2 book. But, I am failed. Now, I ask for helps here.

Your helps are very valuable for me.

Thanks in advance.
####################################################
# generate my data set
x<-c(rnorm(n=50, mean=1, sd=2), rnorm(n=50, mean=10, sd=2),
rnorm(n=1000, mean=1, sd=3),rnorm(n=1000, mean=10, sd=3))
y<-c(rnorm(n=50, mean=1, sd=2), rnorm(n=50, mean=10, sd=2),
rnorm(n=1000, mean=1, sd=3),rnorm(n=1000, mean=10, sd=3))
gp<-c(rep(c("a","b"),each=c(50,50)),rep(c("abackground","bbackground"),
each=c(1000, 1000)))

mydata<-data.frame(gp, x, y)

####################################################
# ggploting

library(ggplot2)
#################################
# the first try.
pp<-ggplot(mydata, aes(y, x, group = gp)) + geom_point()
(pp + geom_point(aes(group="a"), se=4, fill="blue")) # does not work

################################
# the second try.
library(NCStat)
a.data<-Subset(mydata, gp=="a")
b.data<-Subset(mydata, gp=="b")
a.background<-Subset(mydata, gp=="abackground")
b.background<-Subset(mydata, gp=="bbackground")

(pp + geom_point(data=a.data,aes(y, x, color="honeydew3"))
+ geom_point(data=b.data,aes(y, x, color="yellow4")
+ geom_point(data=a.background,aes(y, x, color="cyan")
+ geom_point(data=b.background,aes(y, x, color="blue")))


Best.

Mao Jian-Feng

parts:
Mao, 

Ah, I misunderstood. Looked like you had it mostly, but the syntax wasn't quite there.

# generate my data set
x<-c(rnorm(n=50, mean=1, sd=2), rnorm(n=50, mean=10, sd=2),
rnorm(n=1000, mean=1, sd=3),rnorm(n=1000, mean=10, sd=3))
y<-c(rnorm(n=50, mean=1, sd=2), rnorm(n=50, mean=10, sd=2),
rnorm(n=1000, mean=1, sd=3),rnorm(n=1000, mean=10, sd=3))
gp<-c(rep(c("a","b"),each=c(50,50)),rep(c("abackground","bbackground"),
each=c(1000, 1000)))

mydata<-data.frame(gp, x, y)

####################################################
# ggploting

library(ggplot2)

a.data<-subset(mydata, gp=="a")
b.data<-subset(mydata, gp=="b")
a.background<-subset(mydata, gp=="abackground")
b.background<-subset(mydata, gp=="bbackground")

ggplot()+
geom_point(data=a.background,aes(x=x, y=y), color="grey70") +
geom_point(data=b.background,aes(x=x, y=y), color="grey50")+
geom_point(data=a.data,aes(x=x, y=y), color="red") +
geom_point(data=b.data,aes(x=x, y=y),  color="blue")

#####END CODE ####


The layer order is important for what you want to accomplish. The "a" and "b" layers come last, otherwise they get overplotted. 

Does that work? 

Brandon
